account: HIBA was built by the Humanitarian Engineering Initiative of the American University of Beirut with a Gates Foundation Grand Challenges grant. The HIBA chatbot combines retrieval, language models, speech recognition, and speech synthesis. It supports 28 languages. Testing included groups of 6, 20, and 50 participants, and the team used their feedback to refine language, usability, and content. The team reports that HIBA was being deployed in shelters for displaced people in Lebanon as of October 2024. In a document of 8 May 2025, the team reports that users submitted about 700 queries over six months, often on reproductive, sexual and mental health. The team's account to the International Telecommunication Union, current as of June 2025, describes access and user-testing work. It presents improved health literacy and better health decisions as expected outcomes.
